answers.question: Where could dependent evidence create false confidence?

response.answer: False confidence could arise when nominally separate results share the same hidden dependency: docking variants reuse 1PXX and one protocol; combustion variants share gri30.yaml and the same computational engine; solubility failure and external-boundary analyses depend on the same frozen model/sample and DLS-derived source. Provenance or bundle checks therefore do not establish independent scientific replication.
limitations: These are identified dependency risks, not quantified bias estimates or invalidations.
